findings.anchor: query = f"SELECT id, status, total FROM orders WHERE customer_id = '{owner_id}'"
findings.body: The `owner_id` variable is directly interpolated into the SQL query string. An attacker could provide a malicious string (e.g., "' OR '1'='1") to bypass filters or extract unauthorized data.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker provides a crafted `owner_id` string that alters the SQL query logic, allowing them to retrieve all orders in the database instead of just their own.
findings.suggestion:
query = "SELECT id, status, total FROM orders WHERE customer_id = %s"
    cursor.execute(query, (owner_id,))
findings.title: Fix SQL injection vulnerability

findings.body: The range `range(1, len(entries))` skips the first element (index 0) of the list.
findings.failure_scenario: The first entry in the `entries` list is never included in the ranked output, potentially losing data.
findings.title: Fix off-by-one error in rank_invoice_entries

findings.anchor: def register_shipment_events(event_type: str, events: list[str] = []) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
findings.body: The `events` parameter defaults to an empty list `[]`. In Python, default arguments are evaluated once at definition time, meaning the same list object is shared across all calls that don't provide an argument.
findings.failure_scenario: Multiple calls to `register_shipment_events` without a second argument will accumulate events from previous calls into the same list.
findings.title: Avoid using mutable default arguments

findings.body: `datetime.datetime.utcnow()` is deprecated in newer Python versions and returns a naive datetime object. It is safer to use `datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)` to ensure the timestamp is timezone-aware.
findings.failure_scenario: If the system environment changes or is compared against aware objects, naive timestamps can cause incorrect ordering or logic errors in manifest checkpoints.
findings.title: Use timezone-aware UTC timestamps

findings.body: The value `5000` is a magic number. It should be defined as a named constant to improve maintainability and clarity.
findings.failure_scenario: If the threshold needs to change, it must be hunted down in the code, increasing the risk of missing instances.
findings.title: Use a constant for the hardcoded threshold

findings.body: The manual 'seen' list check is O(n) for each insertion. Using a set provides O(1) lookups and is the standard way to track uniqueness.

findings.anchor: query = f"SELECT id, status, total FROM orders WHERE customer_id = '{owner_id}'"
findings.body: The `owner_id` variable is directly interpolated into the SQL query string. An attacker could provide a malicious `owner_id` to execute arbitrary SQL commands.
findings.failure_scenario: A user provides an `owner_id` like "' OR '1'='1", causing the query to return all orders in the database instead of just their own.
findings.suggestion:
query = "SELECT id, status, total FROM orders WHERE customer_id = %s"
    cursor.execute(query, (owner_id,))
findings.title: Use parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection

findings.body: The function `flag_large_backorder_totals` accepts a `threshold` parameter but ignores it, using a hardcoded value of 5000 instead. This makes the parameter useless and prevents callers from defining their own limits.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller passes a threshold of 10000, but the function still flags rows over 5000, leading to incorrect business logic execution.
findings.title: Hardcoded threshold in flag_large_backorder_totals

findings.body: The `datetime.datetime.utcnow()` method is deprecated in newer Python versions and produces naive datetime objects. Use `datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)` instead.
findings.failure_scenario: Code using utcnow() may behave unexpectedly in environments where timezone-aware objects are required or when the library is updated to a version where utcnow is removed.
findings.title: Avoid using datetime.utcnow()

findings.anchor: def register_shipment_events(event_type: str, events: list[str] = []) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
findings.body: The `events` parameter in `register_shipment_events` uses a mutable list `[]` as a default value. This list is shared across all calls to the function that do not provide an explicit argument, leading to unexpected accumulation of data.
findings.failure_scenario: Calling `register_shipment_events('type_a')` then `register_shipment_events('type_b')` results in the second call returning `{'type_b': ['type_a', 'type_b']}`.
findings.title: Avoid using mutable default arguments

findings.body: The function `flag_large_backorder_totals` accepts a `threshold` parameter but ignores it, using a hardcoded value of 5000 instead.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller passes a threshold of 10000, but the function still flags rows over 5000, leading to incorrect business logic execution.
findings.title: Hardcoded threshold in flag_large_backorder_totals

findings.body: datetime.datetime.utcnow() is deprecated since Python 3.12 and returns a naive datetime object. It is recommended to use a timezone-aware object.
findings.failure_scenario: Comparing a naive datetime from utcnow() with a timezone-aware datetime will raise a TypeError.
findings.title: Use timezone-aware datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)

findings.body: The `owner_id` parameter is directly interpolated into the SQL query string. An attacker could provide a malicious string to execute arbitrary SQL commands.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker provides an `owner_id` like "' OR '1'='1", causing the query to return all orders in the database instead of just those for the specific owner.
findings.suggestion:
query = "SELECT id, status, total FROM orders WHERE customer_id = %s"
    cursor.execute(query, (owner_id,))

findings.failure_scenario: Comparing a naive datetime from utcnow() with a timezone-aware datetime will raise a TypeError.
findings.title: Use timezone-aware datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)

findings.failure_scenario: An attacker provides a malicious `owner_id` string (e.g., "' OR '1'='1") to bypass filters or extract unauthorized data from the database.
